question: Should native cross-gateway session messaging become a core Gateway feature now, and should it proceed through the existing `gateway.peers` PR or wait for the broader federation contract?
rationale: The requested behavior is useful and source-reproducible, but it changes Gateway trust, message delivery, and session-state boundaries in a way automation cannot safely decide without maintainer product/security intent.

options.title: Review a secure core contract first
options.body: Keep this issue open, review the linked PR against explicit peer identity, authorization, session-state, and proof requirements, and land only if those requirements are satisfied.

options.title: Defer to the federation FRD
options.body: Treat the linked PR as premature and resolve this through the broader bridge protocol and cross-gateway identity tracker before adding session-tool parameters.

options.title: Keep it outside core for now
options.body: Document MCP/plugin bridge options such as the community IPC hub as the supported workaround until core exposes a maintainer-approved extension point.

recommendation.title: Review a secure core contract first
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open, review the linked PR against explicit peer identity, authorization, session-state, and proof requirements, and land only if those requirements are satisfied.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has the strongest combined history on session tools and gateway role/trust-boundary code relevant to this decision.
